title: Why Astronomers Fear the Silent Invasion of Rogue Planets
description: What happens if a rogue planet passes through our solar system?

shots.narration: Trillions of rogue planets wander blindly through our galaxy!
They outnumber star-bound worlds by six to one.
Some scream through the void at 200 kilometers per second.
These dark nomads emit almost no detectable infrared heat.
You would have only hours of warning before impact.
The odds of invasion in a millennium are one in a billion.
Even a Mars-sized interloper shatters our gravitational balance.
Violent cosmic collisions originally flung them out of orbit.
Orphaned worlds drift forever unless they drag a moon along.
Sub-brown dwarfs are essentially massive failed stars.
Some wander just 7.27 light-years away from us.
In the Orion Nebula, Jupiter-sized pairs drift together.
There are two rogue giants for every single star.
OTS 44 carries a dust disk ten times Earth's mass.
Gravity warps space-time like a giant magnifying glass.
Temperatures on these drifters drop to freezing depths.
Microlensing reveals their hidden presence in hours.
Their silent approach leaves no thermal signature behind.
A single pass throws entire planetary orbits into chaos.
Earth could be flung entirely into the dark.
Trillions more hide in the uncharted interstellar deep.
Frozen silence claims our world forever.
